text:
maria: Seeing provisioning stalls in us-east1 this morning, ~30% of GPU allocs failing. Root cause looks like local SSD hot-queue on the gnode pool — short, very high IOPS bursts from janitor + fstrim causing long blk_queue waits. dmesg shows intermittent EIOs on some hosts.
devin: ack. metrics quick link: https://graf.redwood.internal/d/ssd-hotqueue?var=us-east1 — can you paste the promql you used?
maria: promql: sum(rate(node_disk_io_time_seconds_total{device=~\"nvme.*\",region=\"us-east1\"}[1m])) by (instance)
maria: also saw `blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector ...` on 3 hosts (gnode-us-east1-22/44/77) in the kernel logs.
raj: pinging storage team to throttle janitor and scrub. @janitor-bot can you report current janitor concurrency for pool-us-east1?
janitor-bot: current_concurrency=48, pending_delete_queue=10234, last_rate_limit=none
lydia: 48 is too high — we had a soft target of 8-16 for this pool. Proposal: throttle to 12 immediately and enable exponential backoff on EIO responses. Pause background fstrim on hot nodes for 30m as a quick mitigant.
noah: +1. Quick mitigation: taint hot nodes so new GPU pods avoid them, then migrate low-priority workloads off the hot nodes.
devin: taint command (will roll out gradually):
```
kubectl get nodes -l region=us-east1 -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl taint nodes {} hot-io=true:NoSchedule --overwrite
```
devin: will also watch pod scheduling after tainting.
maria: also reducing janitor concurrency via ops API:
```
curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood.internal/maintenance -d '{"region":"us-east1","service":"janitor","concurrency":12}'
```
maria: opening a short P0 runbook and notifying SRE oncall.
raj: long-term action: smarter janitor scheduling to avoid co-locating heavy write scrubs with GPU launch waves. Add to infra roadmap and prioritize after stabilization.
lydia: after throttling, watch these key metrics for 15m: `node_disk_io_time_seconds`, `nvme_write_latency_ms_p99`, and `kube_pod_start_duration_seconds{pod_template=~\"gpu-.*\"}`. Also check SMART `reallocated_sectors` on suspect hosts.
noah: scripted quick migration for low-priority pods:
```
kubectl get pods -n gpu -l workload=low-priority -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl delete pod -n gpu --grace-period=30
```
maria: rolling now. will report back at +15m.

(15 minutes later)
maria: update: janitor concurrency decreased to 12, fstrim paused on 7 nodes. GPU alloc failures down from ~29% -> 4%. IOPS bursts much reduced. One host (gnode-us-east1-77) still shows persistent EIOs, marked as cull candidate.
devin: added alert `nvme_eio_count > 5` in 10m to trigger auto-cull. Also drafting a canary change to default-throttle janitor when `pending_delete_queue > 5k`.
raj: good work. Postmortem items: implement soft-rate-limits in janitor scheduler, add handshake so scrubs/backfills backoff when pod-launch queue > threshold, and extend node-level hot-io labeling.
lydia: scheduling a 2h blameless postmortem tomorrow 10:00 US/Eastern. Agenda: root cause, mitigation effectiveness, short-term patches, long-term design.
maria: thanks all. :thumbsup:
